intent.note: Clause: 'Add one sentence to each surface (or to verbs-in-full.md and point the others at it) stating the refusal and its two remedies, and a CHANGELOG entry'. Diff: adds a paragraph to reference/verbs-in-full.md, one sentence to the README /audit:task row, and an Unreleased/Changed CHANGELOG entry. commands/task.md, which carries the quoted '--gate-clear for none' at line 39, is untouched and has no pointer. The executor's claim describes the diff accurately (it says task.md was left byte-identical because of the ceiling), and the ceiling is real (7989/8000 read by measure-context.py --gate in the task tree), so the divergence is a forced, disclosed narrowing rather than an error. The new text matches audit-task.py. _owed_case_gate_refusal fires when tests.mode is in _OWES_CASE_MODES (tdd, regression: TESTS_MODE minus gate-only) and gate_cleared (gateBasis cleared). It is called from add (the mode may be derived from the title by _change_kind_discipline), from the --from-file batch add, from scope (judged on the block the call leaves, so --gate-clear and --tests-mode over a cleared gate both refuse) and from done (before either close arm). Each refusal ends 'Nothing written'. Add/scope remedies are '--gate <command>' or '--tests-mode gate-only'. done's remedy is the gate only, and the docs say only that done refuses to close until a gate runs the case, which is true. The docs claim no more than the code does.
